narrative:
Your application was denied because the model assessed an 86% chance that you would default on the loan—a very high risk. In other words, the pattern of your financial profile closely matches customers who fail to repay, so approving the loan would not be responsible.

The three strongest reasons for this decision were your checking account status, your credit history, and your property situation. The most influential factor was your checking account: it was overdrawn (below zero), a condition found in only about 12.6% of approved applicants. This strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Your property situation was also significant—you have no known assets or property, which is rare among approved borrowers (only 7.8% lack any property). This further increased your risk. Interestingly, your credit history of having paid all past credits at the bank normally helps, and it is a rare pattern (only 2.9% of approved applicants have it). However, in your case, this factor still nudged the prediction slightly toward bad credit rather than protecting you from the other negatives—likely because the model sees it as less informative than your current financial strain.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on rebuilding a positive checking account balance and keeping it stable over several months. If possible, build up some form of savings or property—even a car or a life insurance policy—as collateral. Also consider applying for a smaller loan with a longer repayment period or involving a co-applicant or guarantor. These steps will show lenders a stronger safety net and likely shift future decisions in your favor.
